liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Terrapin Station** (2 reviews): Truckin'>Terrapin>jam into Drumz is energetic for 1991; Band added Terrapin after Truckin' rather than heading to drums, and extended the jam at its end [15][19]
- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): Unlike many post-Brent closers, this Throwing Stones>Not Fade Away has energy, especially the Not Fade Away; After Wharf Rat they added Throwing Stones and Not Fade Away; this version isn't a throwaway [15][19]
- **Picasso Moon** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Picasso Moon as a surprisingly strong, shredding highlight of the first set [11]
- **Eyes of the World** (1 review): Reviewer calls Eyes of the World outstanding, alongside the opening Help>Slipknot>Franklin's [18]
- **Knockin' on Heaven's Door** (1 other source): Final five minutes of Knockin' On Heaven's Door are patched from a cassette master [4]

## The recordings

- **gd91-05-05.sbd.hinko.19181.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 185 min; rated 3.36/5 by 14 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the sound nice and describes a stripped-down, living-room feel without the keyboard parts; Reviewer describes it as an excellent-sounding digital soundboard [10][13]
- **gd1991-05-05.150702.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 190 min [2]
- **gd1991-05-05.schoeps-sbd.ed.9367.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 177 min [7]. Said about its sound: An unidentifiable noise at 1:07, resembling a child's voice, is audible on the recording [7]
- **gd1991-05-05.150666.sbd.healy-pearson.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 20 songs; 190 min [3]

## Around the show

- Band seemed reluctant to leave the stage after Truckin'; reviewer in the crowd mentally urged them to play one more [8]
- Hot, sunny day around 90 degrees; reviewer says it was the first Help>Slipknot>Franklin's played at Cal Expo [11]
- Reviewer sat on a blanket second row back from Garcia and had taken psychedelics before the show [16]
- Reviewer notes Hornsby was absent from this post-Brent show [18]
- From Terrapin Station onward, the setlist matches 6/25/88, including the same final six songs in order [9]
- Reviewer calls it nearly the maximum jam show of the era, with very high energy [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd91-05-05.sbd.hinko.19181.sbeok.shnf**: source: DSBD > CD > EAC > SHN [1]. Also: Digital soundboard to CD, then EAC, then SHN; EAC/SHN work by Darryl Hinko [1]
- **gd1991-05-05.150702.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  October 3, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [2]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several masters combined to complete the show; 16-bit, 44.1 kHz [2]
- **gd1991-05-05.schoeps-sbd.ed.9367.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by eD; source: Set 1: AUD:Schoeps CMC-34's>DAT>CDR Set 2: SBD>DAT>C>DAT>CDR; Missing Encore [7]
- **gd1991-05-05.150666.sbd.healy-pearson.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  October 3, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1991-05-05 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1991-05-05-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [21]
